headline: Manchester City 3-2 Ipswich, Brentford 1-2 Liverpool, and more: Football clockwatch - as it happened
body: Fulham secured a first win of the season against a dismal Hull, while Liverpool came from behind to beat nine-man Brentford Andy Hunter’s match report from the Hill Dickinson is here, and you can find it below. Chelsea have returned from the international break with an authority that augurs well for Xabi Alonso. A brace from Pedro Neto condemned Everton to an inaugural defeat of the season as the visitors climbed to fourth on the back of their first Premier League clean sheet since January. A head injury sustained by Emi Martínez, who was carried off on a stretcher after seven minutes of treatment, was the only concern from a mature display in the Merseyside sunshine for Alonso’s team. There were goalkeeping issues at both ends of the field with Jordan Pickford unconvincing for the second week in succession as David Moyes’ side suffered self-inflicted wounds. But Everton could have no complaints about the merits of Chelsea’s victory given their contrasting performances in the second half. Continue reading...
